description: Constitution §0.45 The "-First" Doctrine — the ONE canonical declaration of KYE's build-order primacy law. CEO directive (2026-07-12): the entire KYE ecosystem must be agentic-first, api-first, ai-first, schema-first, machine-readable-first, callable-first, discoverable-by-agents-first, dictionary-first, manifest-first, cloudflare-first, stripe-first, entity-first, registry-first, governed-and-governable-first — all constitutional principles. §0.45 UNIFIES them (§0.10 graft, the §0.42/§0.44 pattern) into ONE ordered doctrine, NOT fourteen parallel clauses (which would be §0 + §0.10). At design time the canonical artefacts land FIRST, in order — schema -> dictionary -> registry -> manifest -> OpenAPI (api-first) — before the code that consumes them; and every artefact is agentic-first, callable-first, discoverable-by-agents-first, machine-readable-first, entity-first, cloudflare-first, stripe-first, and governed-and-governable-first. Every primitive binds the EXISTING chapter it projects + the EXISTING enforcing gate that already makes 'code without its canonical-first artefact' mechanically fail. Only api-first and the ordering framing are genuinely NEW named contributions; all other primitives are explicit graft-citations. Enforced by scripts/gates/first-doctrine-canonical.mjs. EXTENDED 2026-09-08 (CEO directive, thirty-five '-first' primitives named in one message: NAMESPACE-FIRST leads): namespace-first is build-order step 1 — the ID class, schema family or package registry an identifier lives in is declared before anything is named inside it; every primitive now records the ONE canonical root that owns its concept (`root`, resolved through canonical-paths) or declares the measured gap on the row (`root_gap`, §0.62(c)); decoupled-first (external systems are governed SUBJECTS, never hard-coded dependencies of the entity / estate / ledger) and bidirectional-first (the entity / estate / ledger never assumes communication is only inbound) are grafted onto §0.61 · §0.47 · §51 · §75 · §38 · §48. Still ONE ordered doctrine, not forty-three siloes.

publication_rule.rationale: The doctrine (§0.45) is public; this map's enforcer wiring (which internal gate enforces each primitive) is operational self-governance metadata, kept internal like the §0.44 assurance-plane and §0.43 enforcer-scopes registries.

primitives.question: Does every mutable resource refuse a write unless the caller satisfies the resource's DECLARED concurrency policy at t=0 — one current writer under a time-bounded, fenced lease (or a matching state hash for optimistic writers), unlimited authorised readers, every lock attributable, every override evidenced, every stale writer rejected?
primitives.grafts: §0.30.1 admission lease (kye.lease.v1 — a verdict bounded in time, sealed, revocable) + §0.37 t=0 + §16 Durable Objects (the single-writer owner of a resource) + §36 approval modes (force-unlock) + the existing legal-hold / data-preserve action classes (holds) + §0.11 / §0.35 (attribution fields policy-controlled) + CEO 2026-09-08 (lock / concurrency as a first-class rail: lease not lock, fencing tokens, gateway-enforced, custody-of-edit trail, governed force unlock, lock modes, optimistic + pessimistic)
primitives.root_gap: No canonical root owns write-concurrency yet: kye.lease.v1 is the admission lease (a decision bounded in time) and carries no resource, holder, mode or fencing token; no dictionary declares lock modes; no registry declares a concurrency policy per resource class; nothing declares a fencing token, an ETag / If-Match or a 423 response (measured 2026-09-08 across the specs, the constitution and the runtime). Owed, contract-first (task #89): the lock-mode dictionary → the kye.lease.v1 extension (resource · holder · mode · fencing_token · session fingerprint) → one concurrency-policy registry (rows per resource class and sector pack: mode · lease TTL · override authority · fingerprint policy) → the lock action classes (acquire · renew · release · force-release · transfer) → the lock.* event family → the Lock Rail as one §40 concept on a per-resource Durable Object → the lease + fence check as one step of the existing PEP. The three gates bound here enforce the t=0, real-engine and WORM properties every lock event must already satisfy; the concurrency check itself is not yet enforced.
primitives.note: Decision-group primitive. lock-first and lease-first FOLD here (one concept, two mechanisms — three rows would be the parallel-doctrine explosion §0.45 forbids). Pessimistic (exclusive lease, humans and long workflows) and optimistic (state_hash / If-Match → 409, agents and APIs) are two admissible policies of ONE primitive. A fencing token is issued by the resource's single-writer Durable Object, monotonic per resource, and travels INTO the ledger commit so replay can prove the write was fenced. Cerbos and any other policy engine remain a PORT into the KYE PDP (policy-engine-adapter-canonical), never the deciding step above the lock rail.

ladder_groups.meaning: what a thing IS before it is shaped
the artefacts that declare it, in landing order
the external law it binds to, stated honestly
how it crosses, both ways, owned one way
how authority is exercised over it
how it moves through the estate
how it is seen and consumed
the platform bindings it runs on

ladder_note: LOCKED ORDER (2026-09-08, CEO: 'order at your complete discretion — lock what is needed / must have / essential / fundamental'; the CEO's own sequence of the same day was a sample of thinking aloud). Ten groups, each answering one question in the order the questions must be answered: IDENTITY (what a thing is: namespace · entity) → CANON (the artefacts that declare it, in landing order: canonical · vocabulary · dictionary · schema · contract · registry · manifest · api) → REGIME (the external law it binds to, stated honestly under §70: jurisdiction · regulatory · framework · standards · compliance) → BOUNDARY (how it crosses, both ways, owned one way: decoupled · bidirectional · event · gateway) → DECISION (how authority is exercised over it: policy · invariant · deterministic · t0 · concurrency · governed-and-governable · enforcer) → FLOW (how it moves: rail · workflow · pipeline · lifecycle) → RECORD (what remains at emission: evidence · audit · worm · reporting) → FINALITY (how a fact becomes final: clearing · reconciliation · resolution · settlement) → PROJECTION (how it is seen and consumed: graph · query · machine-readable · discoverable · callable · agentic) → SUBSTRATE (cloudflare · stripe). Two deliberate departures from the sample: the dictionary lands before the schema (a schema enum is a projection of dictionary terms, asserted byte-equal by action-class-canonical — the 2026-09-08 `benefits` plane finding), and clearing precedes reconciliation → resolution → settlement (clearing is admissibility BEFORE the act; the other three are the post-observation order). Governing principle of the boundary group: BIDIRECTIONAL COMMUNICATION, UNIDIRECTIONAL AUTHORITY — every fact has exactly one authoritative source and one conflict rule; an observation never mutates canonical state; transport is governed at t=0 through an atomic ledger commit over state + outbound event (outbox → queue → connector worker). A declared timeout (kye.agent.workflow.v1 step.timeout_ms) is the one wait contract, reused by the finality lane for 'confirmation never arrived'. Essentiality: fundamental = identity · canon · regime · boundary · decision · record · finality; structural = flow · projection; substrate = cloudflare · stripe.
